newsitem.title: THAILAND: One Holding resumes trading, no interest.
newsitem.headline: One Holding resumes trading, no interest.

text.p: Investors struggled to sell stocks of One Holding Plc, which resumed trading on Monday after a period of suspension, traders said.
The stock fell by the 10 percent daily limit soon after the opening and was down 0.20 baht at 2.50 baht.
There were with no bids on around 2.24 million shares offered at a 10 percent floor price of 2.50 baht per share, traders said.
"The offering by One Holding is being made but it seems that that investors were not interested," one broker said.
Troubled One Holding said last week it was saddled with debts totalling over 7.0 billion baht and had defaulted on some bills of exchange recently.

One Holding earlier this month said it had defaulted on three bills of exchange worth a total of $13.5 million and owed a further 7.018 billion baht ($270 million) in bonds and loans to 38 financial institutions.

"The most important problem facing One Holding now is about its debts which the company needs to solve urgently. Because of its liquidity problems, investors should stay away from its stock," Thaneit Khantigaroon of Ekachart Finance and Securities told Reuters.
Brokers and analysts said the company would need time to find resources to be able to repay its debts.
One Holding closed at its highest on December 30, 1993 when it was at 155 baht apiece.
The plight of One Holding came to light after Finance One Plc, once the largest finance firm in Thailand, had to see off its own liquidity woes by merging with Thai lender Thai Danu Bank Plc.
One Holding now employs between 200-300 staff. Executives, who asked not to be named, said last week that talks were underway to determine how many jobs would have to go.
